criteria.commensurate: On the main leg yes (18.4 -> 18.0 s). On the scaling legs (+9.6% at 10hh, +5.0% at 40hh, seeds up to +20%) only partly: settle_field costs 0.26-1.57 s per brook seed, and the largest crossed seed (40hh/25 +20%) is NOT the field way but a 12x blow-up of the notice-board siting search (_fits 1,502 -> 18,749; notice 0.27 -> 1.97 s) that no one has examined.
criteria.necessary: Yes. The GM asked for both pre-seating ways gone (specs/320/request.md); the field way must still be drawn, and with settle_field disabled at the end commit 8 of 9 grown legs refuse ('the field unreached'). The search after the houses is required work; the homesteads stage got cheaper for it (main seeds -0.1 to -0.5 s), so the main leg is -2.2% net.
criteria.no_way_around: No - a cheaper way exists and was measured. checks.ford_crossing rescans every brook leg with seg_dist for the chosen ford's nearest leg on EVERY network sample point (703k seg_dist calls, ~half of settle_field's profile at 10hh/39), though that leg is constant per ford; field_runs also computes ford_crossing for all sample points before any is judged. Memoizing the leg per ford alone (same output, same houses and field ways) cut settle_field 0.56 -> 0.33 s (seed 39), 0.92 -> 0.49 s (10hh/39), 1.13 -> 0.65 s (40hh/4), 1.57 -> 1.14 s (40hh/39). Further: the brook-crossing test is a linear any() over legs (247k segments_cross), settle_field runs and draws twice on 10hh/39, and the notice search growth is undiagnosed.

note: Reviewer's numbers: worktrees at c817f9387 and 1c0cc474b, two reps per leg, scratch scripts cf.py/memo.py/prof.py. Not a case for restoring the reservation (main leg is faster without it, per the GM's 'only if significantly faster'); a case for fixing ford_crossing's per-candidate scan and diagnosing the notice siting before the work proceeds.
